windows-autopatch.title: Windows Autopatch overview – Microsoft Learn
windows-autopatch.notes: Windows Autopatch is a cloud service that automates updates for Windows, Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise, Microsoft Edge and Microsoft Teams. Its goals are keeping devices current for security, adopting new features quickly, reducing routine IT effort and limiting disruption. Updates roll out through successive deployment rings, and reliability and compatibility signals feed into the rollout. After a device is registered, the Intune admin center exposes role-based access control, update rings, and Autopatch groups, which bundle Microsoft Entra groups with update policies. Covered areas include quality updates, hotpatch (monthly security updates without a restart), feature updates, driver and firmware updates, and reporting with device alerts. The stated aims are at least 95 percent of up-to-date devices on the latest quality update and at least 90 percent of eligible devices on a supported Monthly Enterprise Channel build. Intended licensing covers Business Premium, A3+, E3+ and F3, and support requests to the service engineering team require E3+ or F3. The service only delivers updates to registered devices, and the targets are objectives rather than guarantees.

azure-artifacts.title: Get started with Azure Artifacts – Microsoft Learn
azure-artifacts.notes: Azure Artifacts lets developers manage all of their dependencies from a single feed inside Azure DevOps. A feed is a repository for storing, managing and sharing packages within a team, across organizations, or publicly for existing public projects. Supported package types are NuGet, dotnet, npm, Maven, Gradle, Python, Cargo and Universal Packages. Teams can publish packages, consume them from internal or external feeds, and install from public registries such as nuget.org, npmjs.com or Maven Central. Access is governed by a feed's visibility and scope, and upstream sources can be enabled to pull in packages from public sources. Creating a feed means opening the Artifacts area of a project, choosing Create Feed, and setting name, visibility, scope and optional upstream sources. Azure DevOps Services supports all eight types, Server 2022 lacks Universal Packages, and Server 2020 lacks both Cargo and Universal Packages. Each organization gets a free storage allowance described as a trial tier, and the limit can be raised. Usage is visible per organization and project, broken down by artifact type.

azure-elastic-san.title: What is Azure Elastic SAN? – Microsoft Learn
azure-elastic-san.notes: Azure Elastic SAN is a fully integrated storage area network offering that simplifies provisioning, scaling and managing a SAN, with built-in cloud capabilities such as high availability. It targets performance-heavy workloads and large databases, and it can serve as shared backend storage for Azure Virtual Machines, Azure VMware Solution and Azure Kubernetes Service. Consolidating many IO-intensive workloads onto one SAN, instead of managing storage per compute resource, can be more cost-efficient. The model has three levels: the Elastic SAN itself, where redundancy and provisioned capacity are set; volume groups, which pass settings such as virtual network rules to their volumes; and volumes, which are partitions of capacity attached to clients over iSCSI. Performance is shared across all volumes, so they typically do not need to be overprovisioned, and a single volume can reach up to 80,000 IOPS depending on SAN limits and its size. Supported features include encryption at rest, LRS or ZRS redundancy, private endpoints, VNet-restricted access and snapshots. Encryption in transit and soft delete are not supported. The performance figures are upper bounds, not guarantees.

azure-lighthouse.title: What is Azure Lighthouse? – Microsoft Learn
azure-lighthouse.notes: Azure Lighthouse enables multitenant management with greater automation and governance across resources, and it is a non-regional service. Service providers can manage resources for their customers from their own tenant, while customers keep control over who has access, which resources are reachable and what actions are permitted. Azure Delegated Resource Management lets customers delegate subscriptions or resource groups to users and roles in the managing tenant and revoke that access at any time. The Azure portal offers a My customers view for cross-tenant information and a Service providers view where customers review delegations. Onboarding can use ARM templates or managed service offers published in the Microsoft Marketplace, and the activity log in the customer tenant shows who made changes. Services such as Azure Policy, Microsoft Sentinel and Azure Arc work with it. There is no extra cost, any Azure customer or partner can use it, and EA, CSP and pay-as-you-go licensing are supported. Delegation across a national cloud and the public cloud, or between two national clouds, is not possible, and Microsoft 365 Lighthouse is a separate offering.

azure-queue-storage.title: Introduction to Azure Queue Storage – Microsoft Learn
azure-queue-storage.notes: Azure Queue Storage is a service for storing large numbers of messages, reachable from anywhere through authenticated HTTP or HTTPS calls. Queues are commonly used to build a backlog of work that is processed asynchronously, as in the web-queue-worker architecture style. All access goes through an Azure storage account. A queue holds a set of messages, and its name must consist of lowercase letters. A message can be in any format and up to 64 KB in size. A queue can hold millions of messages, limited only by the total capacity of the storage account. Message time-to-live defaults to seven days; for service versions from 2017-07-29 onward it can be any positive number or -1 to indicate the message never expires, while earlier versions cap it at seven days. Queue endpoints follow the pattern of storage account name, the queue service host name and the queue name. The page does not cover pricing, delivery ordering guarantees or resilience details.

azure-sql-managed-instance.title: What is Azure SQL Managed Instance? – Microsoft Learn
azure-sql-managed-instance.notes: Azure SQL Managed Instance is a fully managed platform-as-a-service database engine that always runs on the latest stable SQL Server Database Engine with a patched operating system. It is described as having near-complete feature compatibility with current SQL Server Enterprise Edition and is single-tenant with native virtual network integration. Its main purpose is lift-and-shift migration of on-premises or IaaS workloads with few application changes, while automated patching, updates and backups reduce administration. Features include automatic backups with point-in-time restore, local redundancy with optional zone redundancy, the Managed Instance link for syncing with SQL Server, SQL Server Agent, linked servers, cross-database queries, and security options such as TDE, Always Encrypted and Microsoft Entra authentication. Service tiers are General Purpose and Business Critical, and billing covers compute, storage and licensing, with Azure Hybrid Benefit available. By default the endpoint is reachable only through a private IP address. Limitations include no built-in business intelligence services, no physical file paths, one log file per database, and restore targets limited to other managed instances or specific SQL Server versions.

azure-stream-analytics.title: Azure Stream Analytics documentation – Microsoft Learn
azure-stream-analytics.notes: Azure Stream Analytics is a fully managed real-time analytics service for processing fast-moving data streams. Results can be used to gain insights, build reports or trigger alerts and actions. Inputs include stream sources such as Azure Event Hubs and Kafka endpoints, plus reference data for lookups, and outputs include Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SQL Database and Blob storage. Queries use a SQL-like language with windowing and geospatial functions and JSON or Avro parsing, and custom logic can be added through JavaScript functions or C# functions for IoT Edge jobs. The documentation also covers time handling, checkpoint and replay, anomaly detection and scaling through streaming units and query parallelization. Jobs can be monitored with job metrics, diagrams and resource logs, developed in Visual Studio Code or Visual Studio, and run on IoT Edge. Tutorials mention capturing Event Hubs data as Parquet, writing Delta tables, real-time Power BI dashboards, fraud detection on call data, geofencing and threshold-based alerts. This overview page does not state licensing, pricing or concrete limits.

azure-test-plans.title: Overview of Azure Test Plans – Microsoft Learn
azure-test-plans.notes: Azure Test Plans is a browser-based test management solution within Azure DevOps that supports planned manual testing, user acceptance testing, exploratory testing and stakeholder feedback. It also connects automated tests from Azure Pipelines and provides traceability between tests and requirements, user stories and bugs. Test work is organized with test plans, test suites (static, requirement-based or query-based), test cases, shared steps and shared parameters, which allow the same manual test to be repeated with different data. A browser-based test runner covers web and desktop apps and can capture screenshots, action logs and screen recordings that are attached to bugs. A free Test and Feedback extension for Chrome and Edge lets stakeholders submit feedback. Progress is tracked through charts, a progress report, widgets and analytics. Access depends on Stakeholder, Basic or Basic plus Test Plans levels, and the Runs hub needs the Analytics service. The older cloud-based load testing service is deprecated in favor of Azure Load Testing, and the page names no quantitative limits or prices.

azure-virtual-machine-scale-sets.title: Overview of Virtual Machine Scale Sets – Microsoft Learn
azure-virtual-machine-scale-sets.notes: Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets let you create and manage a group of load-balanced virtual machines whose instance count can grow or shrink automatically based on demand or a schedule. Running an application across several instances provides redundancy and performance, and individual instances can be updated or maintained while requests go to the others. There are two orchestration modes, Uniform and Flexible, chosen at creation and not changeable afterwards. Flexible mode spreads VMs across fault domains within a region or availability zone and supports quorum-based and stateful workloads, mixed VM types, and Spot together with on-demand VMs. All instances come from the same base image and configuration. Azure Load Balancer handles Layer 4 traffic and Application Gateway handles Layer 7 traffic including TLS termination. Managed disks are recommended for production. A scale set supports up to 1,000 instances with standard images, but only 600 with a managed image, and it does not protect against a datacenter outage unless instances span availability zones. The scale set itself adds no charge; compute, networking and storage are billed.

delta-table.title: Lakehouse and Delta Lake tables – Microsoft Learn
delta-table.notes: In a Microsoft Fabric lakehouse, table data is stored in Delta Lake format by default. Other formats such as CSV, JSON, Parquet, AVRO and legacy Hive tables are supported, but Delta offers the best integration across Fabric services. The page lists benefits of faster queries, transactional consistency and integrity checks, support for structured and semi-structured data, and compatibility with Power BI, notebooks and pipelines. Delta is applied automatically when files are loaded into tables, for example through the Load to Tables feature. The lakehouse explorer discovers tables automatically, including Delta tables linked through shortcuts, and each Delta table should get its own shortcut under the Tables area. Fabric automatically compacts small files, tunes data layout and manages storage. Spark defaults differ from Azure Synapse: the default source format is delta, V-Order is off by default, and Optimize Write is unset, although workspaces created before April 2025 have V-Order and Optimize Write enabled. For very large data volumes or special performance needs, manual optimization is advised. The page does not list licensing requirements or explicit limits.

direct-routing.title: Plan Direct Routing – Microsoft Teams
direct-routing.notes: Direct Routing connects a customer's own telephony infrastructure to Microsoft Teams Phone through a supported, customer-provided session border controller (SBC). It lets organizations keep their existing PSTN carriers, integrate third-party phone systems and retain more control over voice infrastructure. Only Microsoft-certified SBCs are supported, and one or more PSTN trunks attach to the SBC. Signaling uses TLS toward Microsoft SIP proxy hosts, with primary and failover FQDNs, while media flows over UDP and SRTP through defined port ranges; media bypass is optional. Supported codecs include SILK, G.711, G.722, G.729 and AMR-WB, the last only without bypass. Requirements include a Microsoft 365 tenant with users homed online, a verified custom domain that is not onmicrosoft.com, a public IP and DNS record for the SBC, a publicly trusted certificate, and firewall openings for Teams traffic. Licensing involves Teams and Teams Phone. Typical uses are existing carrier relationships, third-party PBX or analog devices, and contact centers. It is not supported in Islands mode, and support for uncertified SBCs may be declined.

dotnet-maui.title: What is .NET MAUI? – Microsoft Learn
dotnet-maui.notes: .NET Multi-platform App UI (.NET MAUI) is an open-source, cross-platform framework for building native mobile and desktop apps with C# and XAML. It is the evolution of Xamarin.Forms, extended to desktop scenarios, with UI controls rebuilt for performance and extensibility. One shared codebase can target Android, iOS, macOS and Windows, and layout, design, code, tests and business logic can be shared, while native APIs remain reachable. The framework offers controls, a layout engine, several page types, data binding and customizable handlers, plus cross-platform APIs for sensors, network status, device information, the clipboard, file picking, secure storage and browser-based authentication. A single project with multi-targeting and a shared app manifest simplifies structure, and .NET Hot Reload and XAML Hot Reload speed up iteration. It builds on .NET 6 or later with .NET for Android, .NET for iOS, Mac Catalyst and WinUI 3. Android code is compiled to IL and just-in-time compiled at startup, while iOS uses full ahead-of-time compilation. Building for iOS and macOS requires a Mac, and platform-specific code can still be needed.

face-check.title: Using Face Check with Microsoft Entra Verified ID – Microsoft Learn
face-check.notes: Face Check is a premium Microsoft Entra Verified ID feature that compares a live selfie with the photo contained in a credential, using the Azure AI Vision Face API. Its purpose is to confirm that the person claiming an identity is that person. It includes a liveness check meant to rule out static photos or 2D videos, and the result is returned to the verifier only as a confidence score. The match threshold is an integer between 50 and 100, with a default of 70. Processing happens in the cloud, and the selfie and liveness data are not stored or passed on to the verifier. Supported credentials include VerifiedEmployee, government-issued IDs and custom credentials with a trusted photo. Verification works only with Microsoft Authenticator on devices that meet integrity requirements. Setup requires Verified ID in the tenant, an Azure subscription and the Contributor role, plus either the Face Check add-on or the Microsoft Entra Suite. Typical uses are help desk verification and access to sensitive information. Photo quality matters, and large changes in appearance can lower the score.

governance-domain.title: Governance domains in the Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog – Microsoft Learn
governance-domain.notes: A governance domain in the Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog is a boundary that enables shared governance, ownership and discoverability for data products and business concepts. It has a name, a description and owners who maintain the domain and its assets. The idea addresses the gap between IT teams that store data and business units that own and use it, and it supports scaling governance as data grows. A domain can contain data products (bundles of assets such as tables, files or Power BI reports), glossary terms, OKRs and critical data elements, the last of which is in preview. Out-of-the-box types are functional unit, line of business, data domain, regulatory and project. Glossary terms defined in a domain can be applied to any data product there, and an access policy attached to a term applies automatically to every product carrying that term. The example given is a term in a human resources domain that marks sensitive feedback data and routes access requests to a review team. The page does not state licensing needs or limits.

iot-hub-message-routing.title: Understand Azure IoT Hub message routing – Microsoft Learn
iot-hub-message-routing.notes: IoT Hub message routing sends device messages to cloud services in an automated, scalable and reliable way. It can route telemetry as well as non-telemetry events such as device lifecycle, device twin change, digital twin change and device connection state events. By default messages go to the built-in endpoint, which is compatible with Event Hubs. Custom endpoints can be storage containers, Service Bus queues and topics, Event Hubs, Cosmos DB, and Fabric eventstreams in preview. Each route has a name, source, condition and endpoint, and queries can filter on message properties, body, and twin tags or properties. A fallback route sends messages that match no route to the built-in endpoint, and a message can reach several endpoints but is delivered only once to any single one. Routes can be tested with sample messages. Once any route exists, data stops flowing to the built-in endpoint unless a route or the fallback route targets it. Connection state events appear only for MQTT or AMQP devices and are reported as snapshots roughly every minute. Adding the first route typically raises latency by under 500 ms.

microsoft-ai-cloud-partner-program.title: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program membership overview – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-ai-cloud-partner-program.notes: The Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program gives partners benefits, offers and incentives, and the membership workspace in Partner Center is where the partnership is managed. Benefits such as Azure credits, cloud services, product licenses, technical consultations, developer tools and marketing assets like badges are redeemed in a benefits workspace. Offers differ by partner type: services partners can buy packages such as Partner Launch Benefits, Success Core and Expanded Benefits, and the Solutions Partner designation, while ISV partners have ISV Success and Marketplace Rewards, and training services partners have their own program. Specializations and Azure Expert MSP carry no added cost but require the Solutions Partner designation. Legacy Silver, Gold, MAPS and LAPS offers are no longer sold, though existing purchases run until their end date. Requirements are program membership, a verified Partner Center account and the partner admin role. Each offer can be purchased only once, upgrades and proration are not supported, renewal does not redeem benefits automatically, and terms generally run one year plus a 30-day grace period. Refunds apply only when benefits are unused.
